name: Guard Recovery from Zombie
summary: Guard recovery after a blocked Zombie pummel restores inside frames and a comfortable guard when the high-leg posture connection has been lost.
description: Guard recovery after a blocked Zombie pummel restores inside frames and a comfortable guard when the high-leg posture connection has been lost.
overview:
The bottom player is already facing the opponent in Zombie, with a high rubber-guard leg connection. The player begins facing the opponent in rubber guard; the reset does not free a lockdown on the opponent's leg.

The bottom player has broken posture and supports a high Mission Control leg. The top player's hand or forearm is still obstructing the intended arm isolation. Release any wrist, neck or elbow loading before opening the high-leg enclosure. Lower the controlling leg through a comfortable hip angle rather than pulling the foot against the knee.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Ben Eddy — the Zombie pummel](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JzSxFvNA5Uo); [Brandon McCaghren — Gogoplata from rubber guard](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wn39-wrfsbs).

attacker.overview:

The bottom player has broken posture and supports a high Mission Control leg. The top player's hand or forearm is still obstructing the intended arm isolation. Release any wrist, neck or elbow loading before opening the high-leg enclosure. Lower the controlling leg through a comfortable hip angle rather than pulling the foot against the knee.

Bring the forearms and knees between the bodies as space becomes available. Keep the shoulders and hips oriented toward the opponent while re-establishing a comfortable facing guard. Check posture, knee comfort and inside space before resuming a sweep or submission attack.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Once the high-leg connection has opened, use a small shrimp with the supporting frames to recover an inside knee. Move the hips through free space instead of pulling a trapped knee sideways.

Treat the failed pummel as a guard retention problem: keep the forearm between the bodies as the knee returns. It supports the hip escape against chest pressure; if the cleared arm is still available, the New York overhook can be rebuilt only after posture and knee space are secure.

flashcards.question: Guard Recovery from Zombie (bottom): What has failed when their forearm stays inside?
flashcards.answer: An inside forearm still obstructs New York arm isolation; treat the stalled Zombie as a guard-recovery problem.

plausible: Head-side grip change after New York
Second leg closes after neck clears
trap: Knee hug after hand reaches the mat

flashcards.question: Guard Recovery from Zombie (bottom): What releases before a hip turn out of the high guard?
flashcards.answer: Unload captured joints and open the high connection before turning the hips for recovery.
flashcards.answer_line: Loaded arm or neck in the high loop

plausible: Only the low foot's mat contact
Only wrist grip; high leg pulls
trap: Only leg grip; arm wrap stays loaded

flashcards.question: Guard Recovery from Zombie (bottom): How can your raised leg return without foot traction?
flashcards.answer: Use the hip to make a free path for the high leg instead of dragging the ankle across a fixed knee.
flashcards.answer_line: Turn hip; lower the supported knee

plausible: Fix knee; pull the ankle down
Stay flat; reach higher for the foot
trap: Flatten hips; keep ankle pulled high

flashcards.question: Guard Recovery from Zombie (bottom): What should fill the space as the high leg drops?
flashcards.answer: The forearm holds off chest pressure while the knee returns between the bodies, replacing the high-leg barrier.
flashcards.answer_line: Your forearm frame and inside knee

plausible: Both hands behind their head
Both feet outside their hips
trap: Forearm in; knee beyond their hip

flashcards.question: Guard Recovery from Zombie (bottom): How should the hip escape relate to the shoulder frame?
flashcards.answer: A small lateral hip movement behind the shoulder frame creates knee room without letting chest pressure close the space.
flashcards.answer_line: Move hips while frame holds the gap

plausible: Drop frame, then move hips farther
Pull shoulder in as knees move away
trap: Move knee first with hips crowded

flashcards.question: Guard Recovery from Zombie (bottom): What restores the base before another rubber-guard pummel?
flashcards.answer: The arm wrap can be rebuilt only after guard structure and posture control are restored, not while the passer occupies the torso gap.
flashcards.answer_line: Posture held; room for braced knee

plausible: Wrist grip regardless of knee space
Foot behind head with hips pinned
trap: Inside knee, but their chest upright

flashcards.question: Guard Recovery from Zombie (bottom): Which lower-body task belongs to this reset?
flashcards.answer: Guard recovery here restores inside knees after an upper-body pummel fails; it is not a lower-leg lockdown release.

plausible: Knees outside; reach in with feet
Raise high leg before near knee in
trap: Knees by chest, outside their arms

flashcards.question: Guard Recovery from Zombie (bottom): What shows the ordinary guard barrier is working?
flashcards.answer: The recovered knee and forearm protect the torso gap, even though the previous high-leg posture control is gone.
flashcards.answer_line: Knee bars chest access to your ribs

plausible: Their chest reaches ribs unblocked
Hands reach head; both knees trail
trap: Knee at outer hip, ribs exposed

flashcards.question: Guard Recovery from Zombie (bottom): Their shoulder beats your hand inside; what is urgent?
flashcards.answer: Rebuild the inside shoulder frame so the top player cannot turn the failed pummel into crossface and chest control.

plausible: Chase wrist over their shoulder
Lift free foot as chest gap closes
trap: Pull knee in; leave forearm outside

flashcards.question: Guard Recovery from Zombie (bottom): Which detail should a recovery drill finish with?
flashcards.answer: A useful cooperative reset ends with the knee and frame protecting the torso, not merely with a released hand grip.

plausible: Loose high leg draped over the head
Free hands, but both knees outside
trap: Knee by hip, outside the forearm

defender.overview:

Retract the elbow toward your ribs through available space, stopping if the shoulder is caught. Raise the chest after freeing the arm and reducing the high-leg control. Do not confuse an arm pummel with lockdown defense or apply twisting leg escapes to this upper-body exchange.

flashcards.question: Guard Recovery from Zombie (top): How can you deny the next hand-clearing attempt?
flashcards.answer: The inside forearm blocks the bottom player's path under your hand before the knee hug can fix the arm outside.

plausible: Hand outside with elbow flared
Both hands reach around the high leg
trap: Elbow in, but wrist reaches outside

flashcards.question: Guard Recovery from Zombie (top): How do you restore the whole forearm as the hand returns?
flashcards.answer: Recover hand and elbow as one arm through available space; leaving the elbow fixed keeps the shoulder exposed.
flashcards.answer_line: Bring elbow in with returning hand

plausible: Fold wrist to chest; keep elbow wide
Clamp elbow; leave wrist beyond it
trap: Lift chest to drag arm through hug

flashcards.question: Guard Recovery from Zombie (top): When is the early hand-recovery window?
flashcards.answer: The pummeling hand under yours signals the early window; recover inside before the overhook and knee hug close.
flashcards.answer_line: Before knee hug covers your arm

plausible: After knee hug fixes your shoulder
Only once their high leg hits floor
trap: After arm wrap, before head regrip

flashcards.question: Guard Recovery from Zombie (top): Which elbow position limits renewed arm isolation?
flashcards.answer: Bringing the elbow toward the ribs restores an inside frame if the high-leg connection permits the shoulder to move.
flashcards.answer_line: Inside by ribs once shoulder frees

plausible: Outside their knee, palm on the mat
Elbow flared; only hand on chest
trap: By ribs, pulled through a closed leg

flashcards.question: Guard Recovery from Zombie (top): What separates posture recovery from a guard pass?
flashcards.answer: After the high connection opens, raising your chest recovers posture; you still need to clear the remaining guard to pass.
flashcards.answer_line: Their knees and hips can still block

plausible: Recovered elbow clears knee shield
Upright spine defeats crossed ankles
trap: Free head means hips past both legs
